title: Positivity and recurrence formulas for oscillatory Gegenbauer Hankel determinants
shortTitle: Even sizes never vanish: oscillatory Gegenbauer Hankel determinants
oneLine: For the complex weight (1 − t²)ᵅ e^(ixt) on [−1, 1], every even-size Hankel determinant is strictly positive for every α > −1 and every real frequency x, so the even-degree orthogonal polynomials behind complex Gaussian quadrature always exist; odd sizes vanish infinitely often.
abstract: Gaussian-type rules for highly oscillatory integrals can be built from polynomials orthogonal with respect to a complex weight, here (1 − t²)ᵅ e^(ixt) on [−1, 1]. Because the weight is complex, the monic polynomial of degree N exists only when the N × N Hankel determinant D_N(x) of the moments is nonzero. Celsus, Deaño, Huybrechs and Iserles (2022) proved that the even-size determinants never vanish for the flat weight α = 0. This candidate proves that every even-size determinant is strictly positive for every α > −1 and every real x, by continuation in α: a Pearson identity shows that adjacent determinants never vanish together (and that every complex zero is simple), and a large-frequency expansion with constants uniform on compact exponent intervals keeps zeros from arriving from infinity. Odd-size determinants have infinitely many real zeros. The same expansion proves the formal degree and leading-coefficient conjectures of Milovanović, Cvetković and Marjanović (2008) and gives complete proofs of the recurrence-coefficient formulas in Conjectures 2.5 and 2.7 of Lyu and Zhou (2026). A ResearchGate preprint by J. M. Ashfaque (24 July 2026) claimed those recurrence formulas earlier; its Proposition 3.1 fails as printed, and this release claims the first complete proofs known to it, not the first claim. An exact Bessel–Jacobi determinant identity, with an unrefereed preprint of Kounchev and Render, gives the critical length (the first positive zero of the Bessel function of order 7/2) for the span of x^j cos x, x^j sin x, 0 ≤ j ≤ 3. Existence only: no claim about distinct quadrature nodes, nonzero weights or conditioning. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

keyResults: Even-size positivity (Theorem 1.1, proof): D_2r(x) > 0 for every r ≥ 1, every α > −1 and every real x, extending the α = 0 theorem of Celsus, Deaño, Huybrechs and Iserles (2022); the even-degree monic orthogonal polynomials of the oscillatory Gegenbauer weight exist at every real frequency.
Simple zeros (Lemma 2.1, Corollary 2.3, proof): adjacent determinants never vanish together, and every complex zero of every determinant is simple.
Odd sizes (Proposition 3.5, Corollary 4.1, proof): every odd-size determinant has infinitely many real zeros, with an explicit first endpoint correction locating the large ones.

Hankel polynomial degrees (Theorems 5.1 and 6.1, proof and exact checks): deg H_n = ⌊n²/4⌋ and generic deg V_n = n(n+1)/2 with explicit leading coefficients, proving the formal conjectures of Milovanović, Cvetković and Marjanović (2008); two exceptional parameter values lower the shifted degree.

Recurrence coefficients (Theorems 7.2 and 7.4, proof): complete proofs of Lyu–Zhou Conjectures 2.5 and 2.7 in their stated ranges, agreeing exactly with all 18 polynomials they list; an earlier ResearchGate claim (Ashfaque, July 2026) is disclosed and its Proposition 3.1 fails as printed.

Critical length (Corollary 8.3, conditional): with an unrefereed rank-three result of Kounchev and Render, the critical length of span{x^j cos x, x^j sin x : 0 ≤ j ≤ 3} is the first positive zero of the Bessel function of order 7/2.

narration: Even sizes never vanish. An Evidence Press briefing. Some integrals oscillate so fast that ordinary numerical rules need thousands of points. One remedy moves the calculation into the complex plane and builds a Gaussian-type rule from polynomials that are orthogonal with respect to a complex weight. Here the weight is one minus t squared, raised to a power alpha, times a wave of frequency x, on the interval from minus one to one. With a complex weight there is a catch: the polynomial of a given degree may simply not exist. It exists exactly when a certain determinant of moments, called a Hankel determinant, is not zero. In 2022 Celsus, Deaño, Huybrechs and Iserles proved that for the flat weight, where alpha is zero, the even-size determinants never vanish. This paper proves the same for every alpha greater than minus one and every real frequency: every even-size determinant is strictly positive, so the even-degree polynomials always exist. Odd sizes behave differently: each odd-size determinant has infinitely many real zeros. The proof follows the determinants as alpha changes, using an identity showing that neighbouring determinants never vanish together, and a large-frequency expansion that holds uniformly in alpha. The same tools prove degree formulas conjectured in 2008, and give complete proofs of two recurrence-coefficient conjectures stated by Lyu and Zhou in 2026. An earlier preprint, posted on ResearchGate by J. M. Ashfaque in July 2026, claimed those recurrence formulas; its key determinant formula fails as printed, and this release claims the first complete proofs known to it, not the first claim. The limits are clear. The result is about existence only, not about distinct quadrature nodes or numerical stability, and one corollary depends on an unrefereed preprint. This is an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate, not peer reviewed or independently reproduced. Published on the fourth of November twenty twenty-six, its paper and evidence are linked from the Evidence Press release page. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.

decisionObject.description: Whether the even-degree orthogonal polynomials of the oscillatory Gegenbauer weight exist at every frequency: yes, for every α > −1 and real x, with simple zeros and explicit degree and recurrence formulas.
decisionObject.scope: Real exponent α > −1 and real frequency; existence only; the n = 3 critical length is conditional on an unrefereed preprint.
